title: Bridge drain misclassification caused cascading tier fallbacks and regional surge
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: On 2025-02-09 a misclassification in the regional drain propagation path caused the routing control plane to mark multiple healthy zones as draining. The smart router shifted traffic aggressively into lower-tier variants and remote regions. This produced a cascading fallback storm that saturated backup capacity, increased latencies for P0 customers, and triggered several automated model-variant swaps. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root causes, immediate mitigations, and longer-term fixes to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-09T01:14:32Z - Monitoring alert: region-us-west-2 drain count spike detected by routing-controller (alert threshold crossed)
2025-02-09T01:15:10Z - Router started moving 40% of requests from us-west-2 to regional fallback pool and lower-tier variants (policy: latency-first, fallthrough allowed)
2025-02-09T01:17:03Z - Autoscaling alarm: dedicated fallback pool launching additional instances; cold-start latency observed on several model variants
2025-02-09T01:18:45Z - Error reports from client SDKs increase; SLOs breached for <service:chat-api> on customer tenants with Dedicated capacity
2025-02-09T01:22:10Z - Control plane confirmed drain tombstone presence for three healthy racks due to stale tombstone reconciliation bug (reconcile window misapplied)
2025-02-09T01:30:00Z - Engineering mitigation: temporarily disabled automatic tiered-fallback policy and pinned high-tier routing for critical customer routes
2025-02-09T02:05:00Z - Manual rollback of tombstone propagation applied and tombstones cleared; draining flags reverted for affected racks
2025-02-09T03:10:00Z - Traffic normalized, fallbacks subsided; started post-incident data collection and trace aggregation
root_causes: Tombstone reconciliation window misconfiguration: a recent change to daemon reconciliation frequency moved the window so that stale drain markers were reapplied during leader handoff
Routing policy evaluation order: the router prioritized tier-demotion rules over regional health checks for a brief window, amplifying traffic shifts into lower-tier model variants
Insufficient guardrails for fallback storms: rate limiting and circuit-breakers for variant swaps were permissive, allowing multiple parallel variant swaps and autoscaler churn
Lack of rapid observability for tombstone churn: dashboards showed aggregated drain counts but not per-rack churn, delaying detection of misclassification
mitigation: Immediate: disabled aggressive tier-demotion policy and pinned critical routes to their high-tier variants until tombstones cleared
Immediate: paused automated variant-swap automation for production-critical teams to stop cascading fallbacks
Short-term: revert reconciliation frequency change and add defensive deduplication in tombstone propagation path
Monitoring: add per-rack tombstone churn telemetry and an alert when tombstone churn rate > 5/min for a rack
action_items: ENG/SRE - Add circuit-breaker on router variant swaps to limit concurrent swaps per route (owner: Evan Li, due: 2025-02-21)
ENG - Add per-rack tombstone churn metric and dashboard; create alert playbook (owner: Priya Patel, due: 2025-02-18)
ENG - Rework routing policy evaluation order to ensure regional health beats tier demotion for >90% of evaluation window (owner: Miguel Torres, due: 2025-03-03)
ENG - Harden tombstone reconciliation: idempotent apply, dedupe by epoch, and leader-verified write path (owner: SRE Team, due: 2025-03-01)
PM - Communicate post-incident summary to impacted customers with timeline and mitigations (owner: Oliver Grant, due: 2025-02-16)
Design - Review Console UX for drain visibility; add per-route drain timeline and impact estimator (owner: Lina Zhao, due: 2025-03-07)
QA - Add regression tests that simulate leader handoff + reconciliation to ensure tombstones are not reintroduced (owner: Rajesh Nair, due: 2025-02-28)
postmortem_summary: The incident was caused by a combination of a configuration change to tombstone reconciliation timing and a policy evaluation order that allowed aggressive tier demotion ahead of regional health evaluation. The most impactful gap was observability: lack of per-rack churn visibility delayed root cause identification. We mitigated customer impact by pinning critical routes and pausing automatic variant swapping, and we implemented both short-term fixes and a set of medium-term engineering changes to make the routing control plane more defensive.
